To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
GFRalpha-1 mRNA expression in rat striatum is maximal during postnatal days 10-14, and that GFRalpha 1 mRNA is present in striatal medium-sized neurons.
the expression of GFRalpha in striatum peaks at the end of the first phase of natural cell death of dopamine neurons in substantia nigra.
GFRα1 mRNA and protein are expressed in medium-sized striatal neurons at the time of maximal cell death in substantia nigra.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of the development of the dopamine neurons of the substantianigra (SN).
understanding the molecular basis of neuronal cell death in the developing nervous system.
the mechanisms that control the development and survival of the dopaminergic neurons in the brain of mammals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
GDNF and its receptor are expressed in the rat brain during postnatal development, and that this expression is regulated in time and space.
GFRalpha-1 is expressed at a time of peak cell death in SN and striatum and may therefore be involved in regulating the death of nigral dopamine cells during development.
GFRalpha 1 expression is not restricted to the SN, but is expressed in the striatum as well, with a similar timecourse.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
GDNF/GFRalpha1 is a neurotrophic system with a biphasic expression pattern in the striatum.
GFRalpha is expressed in the SN and striatum during post-natal development, and may act to influence the survival of nigral dopaminergic neurons during the second peak of cell death.
GFRalpha 1 is a target-derived trophic factor for dopamine neurons of the SN.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the GFRalpha1 receptor for GDNF is expressed in both the substantia nigral dopamine neurons and in the striatal target cells during the period of natural cell death in the nigra.
GFRalpha 1 is expressed in medium-sized neurons in the striatum and that this expression peaks at PND10-14.
GFRalpha-1 is expressed in medium spiny neurons of the striatum at the time when dopamine neurons are dying.
